method: per-gate pricing of the preflight chain: cost reconstructed from orchestration/handoffs/*.json (tool_calls, status, evidence), the Host board ledger (~/.dsh/task-board/ledger-v2.json: card id, execution id, execution result), orchestration/journals/*.jsonl, orchestration/units/*.md, and docs/GATE-CHAIN.md. Requests are 0 by card contract everywhere; no live-path row exists for any card in this population. Benefit side: one offline dry run at RUN-A*'s own flags (0 requests, 0 sockets) measured G1=1154/4320, G2=2880/2880, G3 n=48 < 60.

gates.name: ledger cap (cumulative spent + turns + ceil(turns*68/801))
gates.prevents: a cell that would spend past its remaining quota, before the first request leaves: the per-turn brake (WIRE-CAP-GATE) reserves the slot in memory and refuses at T1.
gates.prevention_evidence: measured, on disk: cap=100 spent=100 headroom=100 -> CAP REFUSED at T1, rc=4, rows=0, transport calls=0 (orchestration/handoffs/WIRE-CAP-GATE.json evidence.zero_rows_on_refusal); RED with the pre-send call neutered: rc=9, rows=3, requests=3, first row T1/turn, GREEN restored: rc=4 rows=0 requests=0 (orchestration/journals/WIRE-CAP-GATE.jsonl). Dry run at RUN-A*'s flags: G1 1154/4320 (1101 spent + 48 turns + 5 allowance).

defects_list.what: the ledger's own known_limit said it DETECTS rather than prevents: a cell could spend past its allocation and be counted afterwards; the per-turn pre-send brake did not exist.

the gate manifest was named cell-<arm>-<stamp>.gates.json at second resolution into the repo's measure/ dir, so two cells started in the same second wrote ONE file and the second silently replaced the first run's admission record (observed as transient rc=1/rc=0 on a live-path probe).

gates.replacement: nothing in-run can replace a pre-spend brake; a post-hoc ledger recovers the count after the spend, which is the defect this gate was built to remove.

live_path_bypass_possible.thinking_off: bypass through the decision expression: no (three operand-validation rounds closed it; 167 hostile rows, 0 admitted). Residual surface: YES via --budget-glob, which narrows the row-file set the brake scans, so a cell that passes it reads fewer rows than the corpus and can spend into the cap; and the cap itself is read from an artefact, not hard-coded per card.
live_path_bypass_possible.thinking_on_auto: same as off; G1 is mode-independent.

gates.compliance_statement: this does not weaken a guard: the refusal is unchanged and the removed element is nothing — exit 4 with 0 rows and 0 transport calls stays exactly as measured, and the residual --budget-glob surface is recorded, not repaired, because repairing it is a separate card.

gates.name: projection (per-turn calibrated wall x turns vs --max-wall)
gates.prevents: launching a cell whose projected wall clock overruns its declared --max-wall; the one shape it actually catches is a thinking-auto/on cell priced at a pooled figure (60 turns auto = 13,092 s against a 3,600 s ceiling, refused).
gates.prevention_evidence: computed, never observed live: no live cell has ever hit this refusal. Measured refusals exist only in tests and dry runs: 48x180=8640 > 3600 exit 8; --thinking auto 60 turns projected 13,092 s at 3,600 s exit 8 (PROJECTION-MODE); today's dry run at RUN-A*'s own flags admits at exact equality: projected_requests=48, projected_wall=2880 s, limit=2880 s, and prints a worst case of 8640 s.

defects_list.what: ok = not (max_wall > 0 and projected > max_wall) allowed --max-wall 0 and -1 as 'no ceiling', so the gate was switched off by its own limiting operand.
the multiplicand was unvalidated: --projected-turn-wall -1 --max-wall 1 printed 'projected_wall ~= -12s source=flag' and invoked the runner.
--projected-from rows whose walls all price <= 0 s produced a p90 <= 0 and multiplied the projection to nothing (or fell back silently); a 1 s ceiling was passed.
non-finite and absurd operands (inf, nan, 1e308) and values so small the projection rounds to 0 s were admitted: validation had been applied to one operand of the arithmetic and not its siblings.
one pooled 60 s/turn priced every thinking mode; a thinking-auto cell whose own calibration said p50 218.2 s/turn was admitted at 3,600 s (13,092 s projected).

FOUND BY THIS CARD, NOT REPAIRED: the projection prices `turns` while G1 bills `turns + ceil(turns*68/801)`. Measured in one dry run at RUN-A*'s flags: G1 computed 1,154 requests = 1,101 spent + 48 turns + 5 allowance, while G2 projected_requests=48. G2 therefore under-projects by the follow-up allowance (5 turns = 300 s at 60 s/turn at 48 turns) and prices no wall clock for a fetch follow-up at all.

gates.replacement: turns x --turn-wall-cap is a bound true by construction and needs no fitted ratio. It is also STRICTER: at RUN-A*'s flags it computes 48 x 180 = 8,640 s and would refuse the 2,880 s ceiling, i.e. adopting it forbids the grid rather than admitting it.

live_path_bypass_possible.thinking_off: no operand bypass remains (every switch-off value refuses with exit 8). A live cell can still walk past the DECISION, not the expression: a positive --projected-turn-wall below the calibrated 60 s is accepted and only recorded as projection_override.direction=optimistic with reason_required=true and an OVERRIDE line; a --projected-from file from a low-p90 arm does the same. Both are declared, neither is refused. At RUN-A*'s own flags the gate admits at exact equality (2880 of 2880) while printing a worst case 3x the ceiling.
live_path_bypass_possible.thinking_on_auto: same override surface, and a larger one: auto/on are priced at the pooled p50 218.2 s, so a cell whose real per-turn tail is above the p50 overruns while the gate prints 'allow'. --projected-from p90 (682.7 s) is available and is not the default.

gates.compliance_statement: this does not weaken a guard: the refusal is unchanged and the removed element is nothing — exit 8, the operand validation, and the printed worst case all stay, and the two measured weaknesses found here (the follow-up allowance is not priced; the bound is not the default) are recorded as the next strengthening card, not applied.

gates.name: prereg (n supports the claim, --hypothesis required, claim=none refused)
gates.prevents: spending a grid on a cell whose n cannot support the claim it will state, and admitting a live run that declares no claim at all ('silence is not a claim').
gates.prevention_evidence: computed, never observed live: no live cell has been refused by G3. Measured: absent --hypothesis -> exit 12 (before GATE-CHAIN-FIX it fell back to PARM-1 primary and ran); --hypothesis none / unknown -> exit 12; H1 at n=48 -> exit 12 naming 60. Today's dry run at RUN-A*'s own flags (48 turns, H1) returns G3 WOULD-REFUSE computed=n=48 limit=n >= 60.

defects_list.what: an absent --hypothesis fell back to PARM-1's primary (H2), so the run was allowed and the no-hypothesis branch was unreachable from the CLI; WIRE-GATES's contract claim 6 ('G3 refuses a run that declares no hypothesis') read as true while it was false.
G3's refusal shared exit 2 with preflight/harness/unreadable artefact, so a prereg refusal could not be told apart from a broken input; it now owns 12 and the scan test balances both ways.

there was no legal declaration for a claim-free run, so a smoke cell could only be expressed as an H# claim, and the rows carried no claim field at all; a smoke row and a comparable row in one arm would have been averaged together with nothing in the data to notice.

gates.replacement: the analyser's own refusals already reject claim=none rows by name (incomparable_claim), so the pre-run gate is redundant for POOLING, but not for SPEND: the analyser refuses after the requests are billed. Nothing in the analyser stops a 660-request H1 cell at n=48 from being spent.

live_path_bypass_possible.thinking_off: the n-thresholds are enforced before spend for H1/H2/H3. A cell can legally walk past G3 entirely by declaring --hypothesis smoke: claim=none, comparison_eligible=false, any n, requests spent. That is a declared no-claim rather than a bypass of the guard (the analyser refuses to pool it), but it means G3 constrains claims, not spend.

gates.compliance_statement: this does not weaken a guard: the refusal is unchanged and the removed element is nothing — exit 12, the required --hypothesis, and the analyser's incomparable_claim refusal all stay; the smoke path is a declared no-claim and is not converted into an exemption.

gates.name: refusal-spawn rule (declared preflight spawns, zero runner_launch, recomputed counts)
gates.prevents: publishing a refusal as if it were clean when it actually launched the runner — the record RUN-A*'s precondition 2 rests on — and declaring a spawn that did not happen.
gates.prevention_evidence: measured with an independent syscall oracle: at exits {2,3,4,8,12} runner_launch == 0, declared preflight 0/1/1/1/1 == observed Popen 0/1/1/1/1, and a /tmp mutant that spawns without recording fails with 'the oracle counted 2 real subprocess.Popen call(s) but the refusal record declares 1' (PREFLIGHT-SPAWN-DECLARE, V-SPAWN-ATTACK-2).

defects_list.what: the rule 'popen_calls == 0 on every refusal' was unsatisfiable: every refusal makes one diagnostic self-check spawn (the runner's own --dry-run at stage 2/7). The rule was wrong, not the counting.
validate_refusal() returned ok=True for a published record with no spawns list and no declaration block: an empty or truncated record passed, and a self-reported validation.ok:true was trusted.

four spoofable shapes survived the first hardening: a truncated record, a declared-vs-recomputed mismatch hidden by ok:true, a deleted entry that flipped 0 -> 1, and two unlisted rejection probes that wrongly exited 0.
D5, still OPEN: the refusal record is not tree-bound, so a record produced by another tree (or another argv) can be presented as this tree's. The cardinality check cannot see provenance.

gates.replacement: nothing: the only alternative to counting spawns is not counting them, which is the defect. The one candidate replacement (an in-process self-check) changes what is being measured.

live_path_bypass_possible.thinking_off: yes, until D5 closes: the counts are recomputed but the record carries no tree identity, so a record from another tree or argv validates. No other bypass observed.
live_path_bypass_possible.thinking_on_auto: identical; the spawn rule is mode-independent.

gates.compliance_statement: this does not weaken a guard: the refusal is unchanged and the removed element is nothing — runner_launch == 0 at every refusal exit stays the acceptance rule, and D5 (tree binding) is recorded as OPEN rather than waived, with SPAWN-RECORD-BIND still running.

totals.rounds_basis: tool_calls summed over the 12 cards whose handoff records them (270) + 22 x the 9 cards that record none (198); 22 is the median of the recorded set and is a stated estimate, not a measurement.
footnotes: WIRE-GATES, EXIT-CODE-TABLE-2, VERDICT-DISPUTE and V-GATE-REPIN delivered record/table work as well as gate work; their rounds are counted once, here, and are not also counted against a gate chain elsewhere.
GATE-OPERAND-VALIDATION is counted against G2 although it hardened all three gates, because the operand class it closed was found in G2's multiplicand.
SPAWN-RECORD-BIND is counted at zero measured rounds: it is running and has written no handoff, so its cost is uncounted and said so rather than estimated.
